title: Cardinality of principal w-localization
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $\kappa$ an infinite cardinal in its universe such that $|R|\leq\kappa$. The finite-constructible-partition principal w-localization $R^w$ of [def-weil-pbc-w-localization] has $|R^w|\leq\kappa$.

source.place: Tag 0976 (remark-size-w); finite-data expansion for the concrete principal-partition construction, with Mathlib/RingTheory/Spectrum/Prime/ConstructibleSet.lean and Localization/Cardinality.lean.

proof.text: Finite lists, finite sets, finite products, and disjoint unions with at most κ indices and fibers of size at most κ have size at most κ, by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-list-cardinality] and infinite cardinal arithmetic. In Lean, use Cardinal.mk_list_le_max, mk_le_of_surjective applied to List.toFinset, power_nat_le, and sum_le_mk_mul_iSup with mul_le_of_le.

Mathlib PrimeSpectrum.exists_constructibleSetData_iff writes each constructible subset as a finite union of V(g₁,...,gₙ) minus V(f). Encode the basic datum by (f,List.ofFn g); this is injective because list length determines n and List.ofFn is injective. The finite-set construction and the surjection from ConstructibleSetData to constructible subsets show that there are at most κ constructible subsets. Encode an index of [def-weil-pbc-w-localization] by the finite graph of its denominator function, with a constructible-subset witness at each part. Equality of graphs recovers both the part set and denominator function; all remaining fields are propositions. Thus there are at most κ indices.

For every index i, IsLocalization.cardinalMk_le bounds each Localization.Away (i.denominator E) by |R|. Cardinal.mk_pi and power_nat_le bound its finite product Stage i by κ, including the empty product. The forgetful functor CommAlgCat R to types preserves filtered colimits, by the existing library instance; Concrete.from_union_surjective_of_isColimit (the representative clause of [lem-pc-filtered-colimit-commrings-elementwise]) gives a surjection from the disjoint union of the stages to algebra R. Step 1 bounds the domain by κ.
